title: The Science Of Consistency
html:
Over the past six months, my life has been a blur of breakthroughs, big ideas, and exponential progress.

I've been experimenting with improvement in all areas of my life — mind, body, spirit, business, and things are starting to come together...

When I first started doing this shit, I reached "The Peak Of Mount Stupid" within a year.

this is also known as the "self improvement autist" stage.

Dunning Kruger Effect

at the start of my journey...

I was obsessed with learning and sticking to self improvement, especially exercise.

and I even had the mindset of "ignore girls, self improvement is better"

I cringe when I look back at it, but i think everyone has had that stage.

I became a self improvement autist.

The only thing that mattered to me was getting my calories in, bulking until I couldn't eat anymore and was on the verge of throwing up.

eating frozen foods from aldi, still frying in seed oils, the only thing that mattered was calories.

This worked to an extent. I gained quite a bit of muscle and strength.

I went from about 60kg to 83kg in a year. (which mostly was fat... but it did put some size on)

— but quickly realized that overdosing on food every night while playing Valorant until 3 AM wasn't going to work. So I started experimenting.

The Optimal (Insert Aspect Of Life Here) Is A Myth

let's use diet as an example.

Over the past year, I have tried, keto, carnivore, low-carb, high-carb, animal based.

recently, I became dogmatic about the carnivore diet... kind of thinking that "this is the only way!"

The reason I was so dogmatic is that I was on a spree of elimination. I was optimizing EVERYTHING to make me focus on my business better.

and my vision was PURELY aligned to that one goal.

so obviously, to stick to the carnivore diet I had a strong belief that "carnivore is right", so I started talking to everyone about it...

Now that I have hit some business success, getting a good amount of members in, I am feeling myself moving from the "Slope Of Enlightenment" to the "Plateau Of Sustainability."

and I realised I'm probably not gonna just eat beef, salt, water and nothing else for the rest of my life...

but I MIGHT do the carnivore diet in these "cycles of intensity" we're going to talk about...

but with this lesson, I learnt some overall life lessons.

Here are my recent realizations:

Balance Is Found Through Cycles Of Intensity

we love to glorify monk mode and intensity.

I love a good old monk mode when you feel pulled to go all-in...

laser-focused deep work, getting a years worth of work done in a month, losing sleep because the ideas won't stop flowing, and riding the wave of dopamine and intrinsic drive

but sustainability has to be taken into account.

If you stay in a state of intensity or optimization for too long, you hit a point of diminishing returns on quality of life.

When I started optimizing too much, life lost it's quality of life.

Things became stressful. Everything outside of my normal routine was seen as a burden.

If I didn't control every little thing about my life, I couldn't enjoy it for what it is.

The Fundamentals (And Your Consistency With Them) Are What Matters.

Through my cycle of intensity, I have reached a higher baseline.

The fundamentals are what you can fall back on when things get too intense.

They are the 'levers' for making progress.

When you feel lost, overwhelmed, or directionless in your pursuit of personal and business development, come back to the fundamentals — write them down.

Life Is A Series Of Science Experiments

Life is about experimentation. Learning what you like and don't like. Seeing what works and what doesn't.

Slowly making small upgrades in the traits, skills, and wisdom that your character holds.

These small boosts in experience and upgrades lead to massive results in the game of life.

Failure is feedback on what to improve. Looping back to awareness — you cannot improve what you are not aware of.

The Meaning Of Life Is To Pass Down Your Experiences

Experiments = experience.

Experimentation is how you find what works for you.

Experimentation is how you form your life philosophy. The mindset that you look at life with.

Money is a byproduct of your irreplaceable value.

so, that's the moral of the story.

you need cycles of deep intensity.

you need cycles of deep rest.

and most importantly, you need a certain baseline you fall back to.

REMEMBER, the most important part of this... is probably knowing how burnout works.

this is the science of consistency.

hope you learnt something.
